items.stem: Which one of the following statements about independence of the judiciary, appointment and removal of judges is NOT correct?
items.answer: Judges can be removed by the President whenever the government wishes.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. They can be removed only for proven misbehaviour or incapacity by a special majority of both Houses.
options: The salaries and allowances of judges are not subject to the approval of the legislature.
Judges can be removed by the President whenever the government wishes.
The conduct of judges cannot be discussed in the legislature except during a motion for their removal.
Judges have a fixed tenure and cannot be removed easily.

items.stem: "The judiciary in India is independent." Examine this statement with reference to independence of the judiciary, appointment and removal of judges.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Judges have fixed tenure, salaries charged on the Consolidated Fund and protection from removal except by a difficult process.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (judges have fixed tenure, salaries charged on the Consolidated Fund and protection from removal except by a difficult process.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about judicial activism and public interest litigation is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Under PIL, only the affected person can approach the court."
items.answer: Any person or group can approach the court on behalf of others.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Any person or group can approach the court on behalf of others.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the structure of the judiciary and the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is NOT correct?
items.answer: The advisory opinion of the Supreme Court is binding on the President.
items.markingKey: (c) It is incorrect. It is not binding on the President.
options: India has a single integrated judicial system with the Supreme Court at the top.
The Supreme Court is a court of record and its decisions are binding on all courts.
The advisory opinion of the Supreme Court is binding on the President.
The Supreme Court hears appeals in civil, criminal and constitutional cases.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on independence of the judiciary, appointment and removal of judges and answer the questions that follow.
"The removal of judges is very difficult, and no judge of the Supreme Court has been removed so far. The conduct of judges cannot be discussed in the legislature except during a motion for their removal. The senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is usually appointed Chief Justice, though this convention was broken twice."
(i) Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'removal of judges' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The procedure for removing judges is made difficult. (2)
items.answer: (i) President (ii) The process by which a judge can be removed only on grounds of proven misbehaviour or incapacity by a special majority of both Houses. (iii) It protects judges from political pressure and ensures independence.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) President (ii) The process by which a judge can be removed only on grounds of proven misbehaviour or incapacity by a special majority of both Houses. (iii) It protects judges from political pressure and ensures independence.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to the judiciary, rights and Parliament: judicial review.
(a) Give a reason for the following: Judicial review protects the Constitution. (2)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "Courts can review only executive orders and never laws." (2)
items.answer: (a) Courts can strike down laws and actions that violate Fundamental Rights or the federal distribution of powers. (b) Courts can review both laws and executive actions.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (a) 2 for the reason – courts can strike down laws and actions that violate Fundamental Rights or the federal distribution of powers. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – Courts can review both laws and executive actions. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: What is meant by 'epistolary jurisdiction' in the context of judicial activism and public interest litigation?
items.answer: The practice of treating letters and newspaper reports as petitions in public interest.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: epistolary jurisdiction correctly explained as the practice of treating letters and newspaper reports as petitions in public interest.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the judiciary, rights and Parliament: judicial review is NOT correct?
items.answer: In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Court held that Parliament can change the basic structure.
items.markingKey: (c) It is incorrect. The Court held that the basic structure cannot be amended.

In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Court held that Parliament can change the basic structure.

items.stem: "Conflicts arose between Parliament and the judiciary over property." Examine this statement with reference to the judiciary, rights and Parliament: judicial review.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Land reform laws affected the right to property, which was then a Fundamental Right.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (land reform laws affected the right to property, which was then a Fundamental Right.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.answer: No Supreme Court judge has been removed so far.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on judicial activism and public interest litigation and answer the questions that follow.
"Critics say judicial activism overburdens the courts and blurs the separation of powers. Public interest litigation increased access to justice for the poor and disadvantaged. Judicial activism has made the judiciary more responsive to the needs of ordinary people."

(ii) Explain the term 'public interest litigation' as it relates to this theme. (1)

items.answer: (i) any person or group on behalf of others whose rights are violated (ii) A case filed in court in the public interest by any person or group on behalf of those whose rights are violated. (iii) It can make the judiciary take over functions of the executive and the legislature.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) any person or group on behalf of others whose rights are violated (ii) A case filed in court in the public interest by any person or group on behalf of those whose rights are violated. items.stem: Give a reason for the following: India has an integrated judiciary.

items.stem:
